the following: (1) The role of cytokines in the pathogenesis of asthma.
the elucidation of the pathogenesis and pathophysiological consequences of T-cell and eosinophil activation, and with the identification of the mediators involved in these processes.
the elucidation of the mechanisms involved in the pathogenesis of asthma, with a view to developing more rational and effective therapy for this common and debilitating disorder.

asthma is a disease of the T-cell/eosinophilia system.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T-lymphocytic cytokines, particularly IL-5, play a central role in the pathogenesis of asthma.
T-cell and eosinophil interaction is important in the pathogenesis of asthma, and that cytokines are the key mediators in the interaction.

eosinophil activation is a key event in asthma pathophysiology.
eosinophils are not just bystanders but are actively involved in asthma and that they are not just a marker but an effector cell.
